CODEOWNERS covers policies/** (Rego rules) but not the prose contract that governs how adopters integrate with those rules.
findings.impact: A PR weakening or removing requirements in ADOPT-001 (e.g., removing the 'no secrets: inherit' requirement, weakening the break-glass three-gate model, relaxing the required_approving_review_count prescription) would not trigger CODEOWNERS-mandated review. Since ADOPT-001 is the document downstream repos follow for onboarding, weakening it degrades the estate-wide security posture without touching any Rego rule.

findings.claim: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md and other WP plan documents are not covered by CODEOWNERS, enabling retroactive spec tampering that rewrites acceptance criteria.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS has no rule for docs/plans/**. Directory scan confirmed 22 plan files present under docs/plans/. WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md is the canonical specification for all 020x slices including 020K itself. D-031 (docs/DECISIONS.md line ~43) records 020K rationale by reference to 'docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020K + §8 (bus factor risk row, line 188) + §14 U-k closure.' The plan is the ground truth reviewers compare implementation against.
findings.impact: A PR modifying the plan document post-merge can retroactively relax acceptance criteria, remove risk rows from §8, or expand out-of-scope declarations. An R1 reviewer in a future fix round would then compare implementation against the tampered plan rather than the original, making a weaker implementation appear compliant. Because the plan is the specification, plan tampering is a governance bypass one level above policy bypass.
findings.mitigation: Add docs/plans/** @jrnb2024 to CODEOWNERS. This also covers PROG-SCP-001 (the autonomous-execution protocol) and other WP plans that define estate-wide governance commitments.

findings.claim: docs/security/branch-protection.md is not covered by CODEOWNERS, allowing the authoritative branch-protection documentation to be modified without governed review.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS has no rule for docs/security/**. File docs/security/branch-protection.md confirmed present. D-030 (docs/DECISIONS.md) states: 'Configured via scripts/configure-020j-protections.sh (idempotent API caller). Documented in docs/security/branch-protection.md. Bus-factor-1 acknowledged: a single GitHub admin (@jrnb2024) can disable these via repo Settings; quarterly review cadence per WP-SCP-020 §14 U-sec-2 closure.' This document is the authoritative record of what protections are live.
findings.impact: A PR modifying branch-protection.md to falsely report protections as more restrictive than the API state misleads human auditors performing the 2026-07-30 quarterly review. In a multi-operator scenario, a bad actor could revise the documented protection state to hide that they disabled a protection at the API level. The gap is lower-severity than SAFE-001 because the doc is informational, not executable, but it is the audit anchor for the quarterly review cadence.
findings.mitigation: Add docs/security/** @jrnb2024 to CODEOWNERS. A single docs/security/** rule covers both mcp-signing-keys.pub (SAFE-001) and branch-protection.md.

findings.claim: output/control-tower/** and output/ci/** are not covered by CODEOWNERS; cross-repo estate compliance reporting can be tampered without governed review.
findings.evidence: Directory scan confirmed: output/control-tower/estate-dashboard.json, output/control-tower/surface.json, output/control-tower/subsystems/returns.json, output/ci/latest-ci.json, output/ci/latest-ci.md all present and uncovered. These feed cross-repo compliance posture reporting referenced in the SCP control-plane architecture (project_scp_control_plane_architecture.md in auto-memory).
findings.impact: In the 3-layer model (SCP policy / ACC orchestration / repos execution), the output/control-tower artefacts are the estate compliance surface consumed by ACC. Manipulating them could cause ACC's orchestrator to present a false compliance picture, leading to incorrect dispatch decisions or suppressed escalations. Lower-severity than findings-store tampering (SAFE-002–004) because ACC reads live SCP policy evaluation, but cross-repo dashboard integrity is still a governance property.
findings.mitigation: Add output/control-tower/** @jrnb2024 and output/ci/** @jrnb2024 to CODEOWNERS.

findings.claim: CODEOWNERS last-match-wins grammar means a future broad docs/** or output/** rule appended after the specific governance rules would silently override them.
findings.evidence: GitHub CODEOWNERS grammar: the last matching rule wins. Current file (lines 10–17) ends with specific rules: docs/DECISIONS.md @jrnb2024 and output/findings/waivers.json @jrnb2024. If a future contributor adds docs/** @someone-else or output/** @someone-else below these lines, the broader later rule overrides the specific earlier governance rules — with no syntax error, no warning, and no test to catch the regression. There is no protective ordering comment or structural guard in the file.
findings.impact: A careless or hostile future PR adding a broad wildcard rule below the current specific rules silently degrades governance coverage for docs/DECISIONS.md and output/findings/waivers.json without any indicator of the regression. This is a CODEOWNERS-specific ordering trap that is not obvious to contributors unfamiliar with last-match-wins semantics.
findings.mitigation: Add an inline comment above the specific governance rules (e.g., '# ORDERING: these specific rules must remain LAST in their path namespace — GitHub CODEOWNERS last-match-wins; any broader docs/** or output/** rule must come BEFORE this block') and/or move the specific governance rules to the end of any future broad-wildcard block. Also document the ordering invariant in ADOPT-001 §12 or a CODEOWNERS.md annotation.

findings.claim: docs/DECISIONS.md CODEOWNERS rule is case-sensitive; a case-variant path reference would escape the rule on Linux CI.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS line 16: 'docs/DECISIONS.md @jrnb2024'. GitHub CODEOWNERS matching is case-sensitive. On macOS (case-insensitive HFS+/APFS), 'git mv docs/DECISIONS.md docs/decisions.md' resolves to the same inode; the working-tree shows the old case in git history. On Linux runners (ext4, case-sensitive), a PR with the file tracked under a different case would not match the CODEOWNERS rule. The file currently exists only at the uppercase path, so risk is low.
findings.impact: An accidental or deliberate case-rename in a PR on macOS would result in the CODEOWNERS rule silently not firing on the Linux CI runner that evaluates the CODEOWNERS check. The governance-critical docs/DECISIONS.md would be modifiable without triggering the required review path.
findings.mitigation: No immediate code change required; note this as a maintenance invariant. If a future rename PR is ever considered, verify the CODEOWNERS rule is updated in the same commit. Optionally add a CI lint step that asserts docs/DECISIONS.md exists at the exact cased path.

findings.claim: The 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 escalation review is a diary entry with no automated enforcement; it will silently slip if the project goes dormant.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md line 64 lists '020K bus-factor-1 escalation review | 2026-07-21 | docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §8'. D-031 records the date. DISPATCH-NOTE.md §slice acceptance item (d) confirms both STATUS.md and auto-memory entries exist. However, no scheduled workflow, no CronCreate entry, and no automated reminder mechanism is wired. The date exists only as a text entry.
findings.impact: If the repo is not actively developed in Q3 2026, the escalation review date passes without action. The bus-factor-1 risk row remains LIVE indefinitely. A future second operator joining the estate would not see a mandatory review trigger; they would need to discover the risk row organically. The documentation is honest about the risk but does not enforce its own re-evaluation.
findings.mitigation: Before or at 020D2, create a scheduled workflow (weekly cron or a CronCreate-based agent) that fires on 2026-07-21 and opens a tracking issue titled 'Bus-factor-1 escalation review due (CODEOWNERS / break-glass)' if no second maintainer is present in CODEOWNERS. This converts the diary entry into an automated signal.

findings.claim: renovate/** rule covers a non-existent path; this is explicitly acknowledged and harmless, confirmed correct per D-031.
findings.evidence: renovate/ directory does not exist in the working tree. D-031 explicitly states: 'CODEOWNERS rules on non-existent paths are no-ops, so adding the rule pre-emptively is harmless and removes a future drift risk where 020F could land without simultaneously adding the matching CODEOWNERS row.' WP-SCP-020 §4 020F slice creates renovate/default.json. No bypass surface exists — when 020F creates the directory, the existing rule will fire correctly.
findings.impact: None. The rule is forward-looking and deliberately placed before 020F. When 020F lands, the CODEOWNERS coverage is automatically active.
findings.mitigation: No action required. Document in the DISPATCH-NOTE that this was verified and confirmed harmless.

structured_review.summary: Seven of nine probe surfaces named in the dispatch instruction identified real findings. The slice correctly hardens renovate/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, and output/findings/waivers.json. However, five MAJ-severity path-coverage gaps remain: docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub (latent signing-key substitution attack, escalates to CRIT when keymat is committed), output/findings/open-findings.json and output/findings/false-positive-summary.json (direct findings-manipulation and waiver-bypass vectors), output/findings/findings-history.json (audit trail tamper), docs/adoption/ADOPT-001-project-onboarding.md (onboarding contract weakening), and docs/plans/** (retroactive spec tampering). Two MIN findings cover output/control-tower coverage and last-match-wins ordering fragility. No symlinks exist; renovate/** forward-rule is verified harmless; bus-factor-1 documentation is genuine and not performative. Verdict REJECTED: MAJ-001 through MAJ-006 require CODEOWNERS additions before the slice can close. Recommended one-line fixes: add docs/security/** @jrnb2024 (closes SAFE-001 + SAFE-007), output/findings/** @jrnb2024 (closes SAFE-002 + SAFE-003 + SAFE-004), docs/adoption/** @jrnb2024 (closes SAFE-005), docs/plans/** @jrnb2024 (closes SAFE-006), output/control-tower/** @jrnb2024 and output/ci/** @jrnb2024 (closes SAFE-008), plus an ordering guard comment (closes SAFE-009).
